Take -5 to hit for +10 damage — the biggest damage line a ranger can take, and Archery style (lvl 2, +2 to hit) buys back most of the penalty. Everything else on a ranged ranger is commentary on this feat.
Bonus-action hand-crossbow shot plus no disadvantage in melee — a third -5/+10 attack every round once Sharpshooter is online. The two feats are one build.

The power subclass. Turn one: an extra attack, +10 ft move, +1d8 on the bonus hit. Umbral Sight makes you invisible to darkvision — which is how most monsters and the entire underdark see. In dark places you are a ghost.

The nova opener: surprise gives assassin autocrits, Dread Ambusher gives the extra first-turn attack, Sharpshooter stacks -5/+10 on every swing. Round one deletes a lieutenant before initiative settles.
The charmer chassis: +1d4 psychic on weapon hits, Wisdom feeds your face skills, free charm person by lvl 5. Mechanically solid and the rare ranger that leans face instead of pure damage.

A swarm that follows you and eats people — reflavor it as anything (bees, ravens, loose coins). Per hit: +1d6 damage, or shove them 15 ft, or move yourself. The utility pick with real damage underneath.
The planar ranger: +1d8 force damage, portal senses, banishing smite at 9 — it sends extraplanar creatures back to their home plane whether they like it or not.
Primal Companion — the TCE rewrite fixed the class. The beast's HP scales with you, it acts on your bonus action, and it re-summons free on a long rest. Reflavor Beast of the Land as whatever fits.
Magical darkness beats normal darkvision — nearly everything in the game sees through dark but NOT through this. Devil's Sight (warlock 2) does. You attack with advantage; they swing blind.
Do not want the warlock dip? One feat buys Devil's Sight outright — same darkness combo, zero multiclass levels. Pick it at any ASI.
One level: your attack stat becomes Cha (which yuan-ti already boosts), plus Hexblade's Curse for +prof damage on a chosen target. Turns a skill monkey into a duelist on the stat he already has.
Expertise x2 — double proficiency on your two best skills — plus Sneak Attack dice on any finesse/ranged hit, Cunning Action's mobility, and Swashbuckler-style free disengages at 9.

The TCE fix for Favored Enemy: mark a target for +1d4 damage per hit (d6 at 6, d8 at 14), free, no slot, but it eats concentration — meaning it competes with Hunter's Mark, not complements it. Pick one.
The best 1st-level damage button a ranger owns: bonus action, advantage on one hit, +1d8, and you stop provoking opportunity attacks. Use it to land the Sharpshooter shot that matters.
+1d6 on every hit against the mark — Sharpshooter hits included — for an hour, movable between kills. The real cost is concentration: do not double-book it with another concentration trick.
+10 to the whole party's stealth for an hour — the infiltration button. Heavy armor, dump-stat dex, whatever: everyone walks in under this.
Reaction: halve fire/acid/cold/lightning/thunder damage and add 1d6 of it to your next hit. The single best defensive slot any half-caster owns — a 1st-level spell that scales forever.

One slot, up to eight beasts under your command — eight wolves knocking things prone, eight snakes stacking poison saves. Objectively the strongest 3rd-level slot; the DM picks the animals, which is its only balance.
Reach weapon plus a d4 butt-strike as a bonus action, and things that enter your reach eat a reaction attack. The melee counterpart of the Crossbow Expert play.
The lockdown pair: stop-on-hit (Sentinel) triggers off the reach attack (PAM), so things that walk up to you freeze in place at 10 ft out. Turns a melee build into area denial.
Rangers fail Wisdom saves constantly and there is no class feature covering it. +1 Wis and save proficiency patches the biggest hole in the chassis.
+5 initiative and immune to surprise — stacks with Gloom Stalker's ambush math. Going first is a build feature: the alpha strike decides fights before they start.
After every rest: temp HP for the whole party equal to level+Cha. Any +Cha race makes it land — at mid levels that is a free life total for six people per short rest.
+1 Cha, mimic voices perfectly, advantage on Deception when impersonating someone. The infiltration feat — enter as anyone, sound like anyone.
Three free rerolls a day, yours or theirs — attacks, saves, or checks. The feat that is never wasted: it converts three disasters per day into fresh rolls.
Eldritch blast for a real ranged option plus Hex once a day — a warlock dip with no multiclass level spent. Pairs with the yuan-ti Cha.
Half-elves and elves only: when you have advantage on a Dex attack, reroll one die — triple-advantage. Sharpshooter crit-fishing goes from good to absurd.
Small races only: +1 Str or Dex, extra speed, advantage to escape grapples — turns a halfling into a slippery skirmisher.
Humans, half-elves, half-orcs: +1 skill, +1 tool, and one expertise. Cheap, quiet, and the single most efficient skill-monkey feat.
Dwarves only: spend a hit die as a bonus action to heal. Your hit dice become a combat resource instead of a rest resource.

The assassin-bruiser classic: Reckless Attack gives YOURSELF advantage on Str attacks — finesse weapons still count — so Sneak Attack fires every turn with no flanking and no setup. Barb 5 for Extra Attack and Bear Totem 3 resists everything coming back. Rage is just gravy.

Smite spends any slot, and sorcerer levels pile up slots — plus Quickened Spell means spell AND full smite-attack routine in the same turn. The dedicated nova machine: one boss round, triple-digit damage, everyone at the table goes quiet.
One hexblade level: attacks run on Cha (drop Str entirely), and pact slots recharge on a SHORT rest — your smite economy refills at lunch. Widely considered the strongest paladin chassis in 2014.
The gish that loses nothing: Cha to attacks, medium armor and shield proficiency from the dip, full bard casting underneath, flourishes on top. All the swordplay, none of the stat split.

Pact slots convert to sorcery points, pact magic recharges on short rest — with enough short rests the loop has no ceiling. The famous infinite-slot exploit. Most DMs cap it; everyone knows it; nobody's proud. Knowing it exists is the point.

Wild shape into a 34-HP bear, rage inside the bear — resistance to nearly everything on top of a disposable HP pool that resets per short rest. The cheapest tank math in the game: you ARE the hit points.

Two levels of fighter in anything: a whole extra action once per rest. On a caster that's two fireballs in one turn; on a martial it's the whole attack routine twice. The most stapled-on dip in the game.

One cleric level grants heavy armor and shields on a full caster — wizard in plate, hit points keep pace with level, and Life/Nature/Tempest each add a real feature. One level slows your spell table by exactly one level.
Bond allies get +1d4 to attacks, checks, AND saves between each other, reaction-free — and it STACKS with bless. Arguably the strongest single level printed in 2014; a lot of tables ban it outright.

Aura of Conquest drops feared creatures to zero movement; wrathful smite or an undead/GOO warlock applies the fear. Frightened AND speed 0 AND they can't approach — the lockdown loop: they can't move, can't fight, can't leave.

Channel: the target's next hit takes DOUBLE damage — vulnerability on command. Feed it to a paladin's smite crit or an assassin's autocrit and a boss loses half its health bar to a single swing. The support pick that makes novas nuclear.
Two d20s rolled at dawn, replace any roll you can see — enemy saves, ally death saves, your own everything. Two stored dice is a whole build feature; the rest of divination wizard is gravy.

A free-standing echo doubles your board presence: attack from its square, take reaction attacks from two positions, teleport-swap with it. The strongest straight-fighter pick — no multiclass required.
Giant's Might goes Large +1d6 damage, and the runes are basically free spells on a fighter chassis — the martial that came with a utility belt.

Samurai's Fighting Spirit is advantage on ALL attacks as a bonus action, 3/rest — Sharpshooter's -5/+10 pays for itself on every swing it covers. Self-sufficient advantage is the rarest resource in the game.
Rakish Audacity: Sneak Attack any duel target without needing advantage — plus Cha to initiative and free retreat. The duelist rogue that never has to beg for flanking.

Bonus-action wild shape plus the CR1 forms table at level 2 — the level 2-5 window where druid is the best class in the game, period. Bonus-action giant spiders while everyone else is swinging swords.

The domain that got errata'd for being too strong: 300-ft darkvision shared with the party, a channel that hands out temp HP every round like a warlock aura — and flight at 6. The safest 'strong' pick in the book.

Find Familiar (wizard list, or Ritual Caster feat): an owl uses Flyby so it never provokes — it lands the Help action on your target every turn and leaves. Free advantage on demand, forever, for one ritual slot. The cheapest advantage engine in the game.

Reaction: force a reroll of ANY d20 — their successful save against your banishment, their crit on the fighter — and grant someone advantage. The single most complained-about spell of the edition. If it is legal at your table, it is always right.

15-ft aura: halves enemy speed AND 3d8 every turn — they cannot leave and cannot stop taking it. Pair with Spiritual Weapon (no concentration) and the cleric has a real bonus action too. The standing blender build.
Bonus action, NO concentration, scales with slot level — the spell that fixes the cleric's dead bonus action and never competes with your real concentration pick.

Plant Growth is NOT concentration — quarter-speed terrain, permanently. Layer spike growth (2d4 per 5 ft) on top and the field grinds: slowed to a crawl and bleeding. The ranger battlefield-in-a-box nobody casts.
Disciple of Life applies PER BERRY: each goodberry heals 4 HP instead of 1 — ten berries, 40 HP of distribute-anywhere healing for a 1st-level slot. The famous goodberry bomb.

Eight pixies, each carrying polymorph and fly: they turn the whole party into T-Rexes, or mass-fly the raid. The strongest 4th-level slot in the game — so strong DMs invoke 'the DM picks the fey' specifically because of it.

The TCE feat: 2 sorcery points plus two metamagics. Take Subtle — no verbal or somatic components. On yuan-ti, the racial suggestion spell now leaves no evidence at all; on anyone it makes social spells unprovable.
+1 Int/Wis/Cha AND a free daily Misty Step AND a free 1st-level div/ench spell — the strongest half-feat printed. Put it on every caster.
+1 to any stat, +1 skill, expertise in anything — Deception expertise on a Cha-forward ranger means a proficiency-doubled face. Cheap and always right.
Advantage on concentration saves plus casting as an opportunity attack — the seatbelt for any build living on a concentration spell.
+1 mental stat, invisible bonus-action shove, buffed mage hand — push people off ledges with your mind and never touch them. Pairs with spikes, cliffs, and lava.
The TCE half-feats: on-hit push 5 ft (off the cliff), speed debuff, or party-wide advantage on your crits — free riders stapled onto every attack you were already making.

The forgotten tech: Slayer's Prey is a class feature, not a spell — no concentration. It stacks with Hunter's Mark for double damage dice on the target and re-applies free forever. Both tracks on one boss.

Hunter's Horde Breaker adds an attack vs a second adjacent target; Gloom's Dread Ambusher adds a bonus turn-one attack. Add a bonus-action attack (TWF or Crossbow Expert) and that is 4-5 attacks on turn one.
Anyone can hold it: bank 5 levels of spells pre-fight — an ally carries your concentration cast, or you store a second fireball. The rechargeable utility slot.
Zero investment: shove a target prone with Athletics, then hit the floor — prone grants melee advantage, and grappled means they cannot stand anyway. The free melee engine, no levels needed.
A pegasus that shares your smites and every 'self' spell — flyby smiting from the air at level 9. The paladin spell nobody reads the second page of.
Store buffs and heals in glyphs as pre-fight batteries — haste keyed to 'when I draw steel', heals keyed to 'when I fall'. Spellcasting as infrastructure.
Bind the thing you just conjured for a day (upcast: months) — your elemental keeps working after concentration ends. The loop that turns summons into permanent assets.
+5 max HP per slot level to three allies for eight hours — a 4th-level Aid is +10 each. The quiet best HP buff in the game; cast it before the boss door, no concentration needed.
The 'no ambush on the road' spells: a ritual hut nothing enters without your say, or a rope-extradimensional short rest. In a plane of ambushers, sleeping safe is a build feature — see Alert.
Ritual-cast free — every animal is a witness and most DMs play them honest. The cheapest intel network in the game; ten minutes of prep buys a dungeon's whole layout.
The TCE style: shillelagh turns the quarterstaff into a WISDOM weapon — a single-stat ranger where max Wis covers attacks AND spells, and you never touch Dex. Guidance cantrip included.
The UA fighting style: unlimited opportunity attacks inside your reach. Pair it with Polearm Master's enter-reach trigger and enemies cannot approach you, full stop.
The TCE race option: +2 to any stat, darkvision, and ANY FEAT at level 1 — variant human except the feat IS the chassis. Start with Sharpshooter or Crusher and the build exists on day one.
Thorn Whip pulls 10 ft; Spike Growth deals 2d4 per 5 ft moved — that's 4d4 free per pull, no save on the drag. Yank the ogre through the blender every turn.
Cast Haste on your party's nova build — its extra action stacks with Action Surge for an absurd burst turn. The classic 'gas the fighter' play, still correct.
Free fireballs for the martial — the DM's gift to characters who don't cast. Ranged AoE with zero levels spent.
Resistance to every damage type except psychic while raging — at level 3. The single best defensive feature any martial owns, and the reason barb frontliners stop dying.
Free revives — resurrection spells cost zero components on you. Dying becomes a resource decision: rage past 0 HP (damage does not drop you) and the party resurrects you for free after.
The melee version of Sharpshooter: GWM's -5/+10 on a greataxe, and Reckless Attack's self-granted advantage pays the accuracy tax every turn. Plus GWM's bonus-action swing on a crit/kill.
Honest barb math: damage resistance IS the damage feature. Take Bear 3, GWM at 4, polearm at 8, and stop theorycrafting nova routes — the class wins by refusing to die while swinging -5/+10.
Unsettling Words: subtract a die from enemy saves as a reaction, and your Persuasion/Deception floor is absurdly high. The save-or-suck enabler — nothing in the game makes banishment more reliable.

Cutting Words protects allies as a reaction AND Magical Secrets arrives at 6 — two levels early. Steal counterspell, revivify, or whatever the party lacks. The original 'steal the best spells' chassis.
The famous theft list: Find Greater Steed (flying mount that shares self-spells), Aura of Vitality (30d6 healing one slot), conjure animals, swift quiver — bard 10+ is legally everything at once.
Half proficiency on EVERYTHING including initiative and counterspell checks — the quiet bard feature. Stacks with expertise picks; bards are never bad at anything.
Riposte (attack back when they miss) and Precision Attack (add the die to a roll — literally pays the -5 on a GWM or SS swing). The maneuvers ARE the fighter build.
Shield and booming blade on a full-attack chassis — +5 AC reaction at level 3 with more attacks than anyone. The defensive caster-fighter hybrid that actually functions.
Mark targets — attack anyone but you and they swing at disadvantage while you punish with bonus attacks. The old-school 'the wall comes to you' tank.
Flurry of Blows riders at 3: knock prone (free advantage for the party), push 15 ft (off the cliff, out of melee), or block their reactions. Control stapled onto your attacks for free.
The honest version: you are not fishing the stun, you are eating legendary resistances — 3-4 flurry stuns a turn forces the boss to burn its saves. Volume IS the monk feature.
Hand of Harm adds martial-arts die necrotic to hits, Hands of Healing heals for the same — a monk that poisons AND revives between punches. The TCE monk that fixed the class.
Pass without trace self-cast, darkness you can see through via blindsight-ish tricks, teleport between shadows — the ninja package, and in a dark plane it's a movement cheat code.
+Cha to EVERY save for allies within 10 ft — the feature that makes whole parties unkillable and the reason 'stand near the paladin' is a real tactic.
Declare the smite AFTER the crit: every smite die doubles on a crit — a 2nd-level smite crit is 8d8 bonus. The tech that makes paladins the nova class: wait for the 20, then unload.
Resistance to spell damage in a radius — half damage from every fireball forever. The oath that makes the whole party hard to magic.
Bonus action: advantage vs one creature for a minute — self-granted advantage covering every -5/+10 you take on the boss. The duelist oath.
The whole cleric list on a sorcerer chassis — heal AND blast AND metamagic, plus a free 2d4 reroll on failures. The strongest sorcerer subclass.
Sorcerer spells cast SUBTLE for free at level 1 — psychic spellcasting with zero components. Charm, suggestion, detect thoughts, all invisible. The mind-control chassis nobody notices using.
Cancel advantage/disadvantage as a reaction, restore-order spells free, and a straight Trance of Order 'no 1-9 on d20s' at 14 — the mathematician's sorcerer.
Quickened: bonus-action spell then a cantrip = double casts. Twinned: one haste or polymorph covers two targets. The two metamagics that broke the edition — take both.
Three sorcery points: the target takes disadvantage on your spell's save. On banishment or hold monster, disadvantage is usually the whole fight.
+Cha to every eldritch blast ray — at 17 that's +5 four times, force damage, 120 ft. THE warlock invocation; the class is balanced around you taking it.
Each blast ray pushes 10 ft — four rays at 17 is 40 ft of forced movement per turn. Off cliffs, into hazards, through spike growth — the blast that plays the battlefield.
See through magical darkness — cast darkness on yourself and it stops being a hindrance, it becomes cover. See the full Darkness + Devil's Sight combo entry.
TCE pact-boon buff: your familiar gets real attacks, poison saves use your DC, command it as a bonus action — the imp/chain lock went from flavor to a second attacker.
At-will disguise self, unlimited — infinite identities, no slot. The infiltration invocation; pairs with every social encounter in the game.
Temp HP every time something hostile dies near you — and things die a lot. Quietly the sturdiest patron; the temp HP never stops ticking.
+2 to ALL saves passively and +4 AC as a reaction — the 'wizards stop dying' pick. The power isn't damage, it's that you never drop concentration.
Dunamancy: +Int to initiative and a reaction that forces any creature to reroll — the temporal wizard. If the table allows Wildemount, it's the strongest wizard school.
The Arcane Ward is a regenerating HP shield that eats hits FOR you — cast abjuration spells to recharge it. The wizard that tanks, literally.
Song adds Int to AC, concentration saves, and your sword fights — the highest-AC caster chassis in 2014. Elves only RAW; most tables let anyone.
Split Enchantment: single-target enchantments hit two targets — twin hold person, twin dominate. Doubling control spells at 10 is campaign-breaking.
Mighty Summoner gives conjured beasts +HP and magical attacks — combined with conjure animals/wolves, your summoned pack actually kills things. THE summon chassis.
Starry form dragon: min-10s on Int/Wis checks and a free attack each turn — wild shape becomes a combat form instead of a scout gimmick. The best non-moon druid.
Summon a fire spirit that teleports your allies and deals damage — a pet with its own turn that also repositions the party.
Unlimited wild shape at 20 — the capstone that turns a moon druid into an effectively unkillable elementalist. The rare level-20 feature worth planning toward.
Destructive Wrath: max damage on one lightning/thunder roll — a maximized shatter or lightning bolt out of a mid caster. The heavy-armor storm tank.
+1 to armor free at 1, fire immunity at 17, artisan blesses the crafting — the sturdy utility cleric that also hits fine.
When you cast an enchantment spell an ally gets a free reaction attack — command/hold person become attack engines. The enabler domain.
Floor of 10 on every proficient check — expertise doubles prof so stealth/deception checks land in the 20s minimum. The rogue literally cannot fail skill checks.
Free half-speed reaction movement when a foe ends its turn next to you — they physically cannot pin you down. The skirmisher package plus free nature/survival.
Sneak attack a second target, soul trinkets, speak with dead vibe — the TCE rogue that turned utility dice into ghost powers.
Psi dice create psychic blades — you never need to carry a weapon, and the dice fund telekinetic movement and telepathy. The psychic rogue.
The CONSTITUTION save proficiency dip — one level gives casters Con save prof plus healing word/armor slots. Paired with War Caster your concentration is nearly unbreakable.
Attack with INT on magic weapons plus a steel defender pet — the artificer that plays like a martial with a robot dog.
A turret on legs: force ballista damage, protector shield for ally temp HP — the artillerist's cannon is a free standing damage+support action.
Enhanced Defense/Weapon scale with level, Mind Sharpener fixes concentration (reaction converts failed conc to success), Replicate Bag of Holding. The infusion list IS the class.
Lightning launcher is a ranged Int attack plus advantage-on-dex-checks stealth armor — the artificer that's basically a ranger with better armor.
Both stack darkness tech: monk teleports shadow-to-shadow while Umbral Sight hides you from everyone else's darkvision — a stealth build that owns the dark plane's physics.
Riposte turns enemy misses into your attacks — on a barb or monk the dip adds a whole reaction economy with three levels.
Subtle psychic spells + Deception expertise: nobody ever sees the charm happen. The social-combat build — mind control with no witnesses.

Devils and similar fiends resist nonmagical weapon damage ONLY if it isn't silvered — a silvered weapon or arrow is 100 gp and bypasses the resistance outright. Against fiend-heavy foes, the cheapest +damage purchase in the game.
An undead or fiend hit by it: DC 15 save or DESTROYED outright — a coin-flip delete on two whole creature types. Even on a pass it takes extra radiant damage.

Throw it: DC 17 or the creature is trapped — and a trapped outsider (fiend, celestial, elemental, fey) can be released to serve YOU for an hour. A pokeball with rules; expect the table to argue about it.
Clamp them on a creature and it cannot teleport or plane-shift — extraplanar creatures cannot flee home. The binder kit: capture it, shackle it, it stays.
A hooded lantern that makes ALL invisible things visible in 30 ft — hard-counters the standard imp/stalker/mage ambush tactic for the price of a lamp.
Scrying at will on a creature you know or have met — one-attunement answer to 'find this specific person anywhere on any plane.' The locate-person item.

Honest warning: 2d6 fire on hit is the most-resisted element in the game — whole creature types (fiends, fire elementals, red dragons) are flat immune. Check the campaign's enemies before buying the shiny sword; against the wrong foes it is a +0.
Advantage on spell saves — which yuan-ti already HAS racially. The rare case where a legendary-tier item does nothing for you. Sell it to the elf.
Periapt of Proof Against Poison — redundant
Same trap: poison immunity item on the race that's already immune to poison. Know which items YOUR build makes obsolete — and pocket the savings.
Fire resistance while held plus cold damage — the sword whose passive resists the most common area element in the game. Wherever fire is common, this is the pick over flame tongue.
Radiant-damage finesse longsword — radiant is almost never resisted, and the sun imagery reads well at every table.
25 gp a flask, thrown like a weapon: 2d6 radiant to fiends and undead on a hit. The peasant's anti-outsider tech — stock it when the campaign turns planar.
Ammunition exists keyed to creature types — a type-matched arrow forces DC 17 or adds +6d10. Buy the type you keep fighting; one arrow decides one fight.
Whisper the enemy's name: it becomes your sworn foe — accuracy and +3d6 against it until it dies. The single-target execution bow; name the boss.
Immune to detect thoughts, zone of truth, and lie-detection magic — the ring that makes your story unverifiable. Pairs with every deception build.
Cannot be found by divination or scrying — the ring handles the mind-reading, this handles the finding. Together you are legally invisible.
At-will disguise self, no slot, no concentration — Mask of Many Faces in hat form for non-warlocks. The cover identity item.
Detect thoughts on a charge — the interrogator's locket. Paired with high Deception, conversations stop being fair.
The mundane infiltration pair: new identities and documents made of paper. In any setting where authority runs on documents, the kit is a weapon.
Pick locks, disarm traps — and where the valuable thing is information, the tools open the cabinet the documents live in.
The famous exploit: hole inside bag tears a rift that sucks everything nearby to the Astral — a one-use teleport-and-delete that most DMs ban on sight. Know it, expect it to be illegal.
The drop exploit: a cube that grows to a 20-ft tower wherever it's tossed — including inside a creature's mouth. 'Fortress the dragon' is a classic; whether the DM allows it defines the table.
Push a button, the rod floats fixed in space holding 8,000 lb — hang midair, bar doors, anchor rope climbs, disable portcullises. The physics-breaking utility item with a hundred uses.
Enemies have disadvantage attacking you — like having dodge on, passively, forever. One of the best pure-defense items; pair with blur-style miss mechanics to never be hit.
Boots of Elvenkind + Cloak of Elvenkind
Silent steps plus advantage on hiding with enemy disadvantage to spot — stack these on an Umbral-Sight gloom stalker and you are not findable by anything that can't see invisibility.
+2 damage on every bow shot, forever, for one attunement — the boring-but-correct ranger item. The damage adds up more than any flashy trinket.
Catch arrows/bolts thrown at you for reduced damage — or fully negate on a good roll. Against the kobold horde firing lines, the glove catch never stops being funny.
A shield that floats beside you — full +2 AC with a free hand. For dual-wielders, archers, and anyone whose build demanded two hands, this solves the shield tax.
Advantage on initiative rolls — stacks with Gloom Stalker's +Wis and Alert's +5 into a build that goes first on every fight. Note: advantage is binary, so one source is enough.
Sets Con to 19 — for casters it locks in concentration saves; for martials it's +HP every level. The 'stop being fragile' amulet.
Recover one spent slot per day, up to 3rd — the cheap spell battery that never stops being useful. Two pearls, two extra smites or conjure animals a day.
A 30-gallon-per-round geyser — knocks things prone, douses fires, fills moats. In a burning plane it's both a firehose and a battlefield shaper.
Daily liquids including ACID and poison — free splash weapon every day, plus infinite mayonnaise for reasons nobody can fully explain. The utility meme item.
A boat that folds to a box — every river, lake, and river-of-doom encounter has a 'do we own a boat' answer, and it is yes.
Eat enemy spells with your reaction, bank the levels as fuel — a staff that punishes enemy casters and feeds your own casting.
The staff BECOMES a giant constrictor snake at will — snake-as-a-weapon, full stop. Caveat: attunement is cleric/druid/warlock only — you need the dip or a sympathetic DM.
Statuettes that become real animals — the serpentine owl version gives a giant owl familiar with flyby attacks: animal companion without Beast Master.
Three fuzzy animals a day pulled from a bag — random, but even the bad pulls are bodies, distractions, and trap-testers. The budget summon engine.
The sneezing dust incapacitates on a failed save — no attack roll, toss it and take the spellcaster out of the fight. The disappearance dust makes the party invisible for repositioning.
Throw it: 5d4 force plus the target gets force-caged for a minute — a throwable banishment with damage. Cheap, single-use, swingy.
Potion of healing — the action tax

Honest note: drinking a potion costs your ACTION in 2014 — the 'bonus action potion' is a house rule nearly every table uses but is not RAW. Craft potions with herbalism in downtime, hand them out pre-fight.

Herbalism kit brews healing potions; alchemist supplies craft acid and alchemist's fire; poisoner's kit brews basic poison (check enemy immunities — whole creature types ignore it). Downtime that converts to resources.
The shield that draws ranged attacks away from your allies to you — pair with Gloves of Missile Snaring for the gimmick build: you are the arrow vacuum.
Resistance to one damage type chosen at creation — pick the element your campaign is full of. A resisted element is worth more than any +1.
+1/+2/+3 to druid and ranger spell attacks AND save DCs, plus a d4 heal boost — TCE finally gave rangers a weapon that buffs their casting.
Cannot be surprised, warns you of danger — on a Gloom Stalker already stacking anti-ambush tools, it's the 'they literally cannot ambush me' package.
Store a spell in the rock, cast it later — an extra concentration-free slot you bank in the morning. The caster's spare magazine.
